records.title: Department of Finance 2026 Pre-Budget Consultations
records.body: Formal submissions take letters or papers with no word limit, alongside an online questionnaire. Open to anyone. The page was published 15 July 2026 and still shows status Open.
records.tip: This is the Department of Finance process, not the Finance committee's. They are separate, take different formats and have different deadlines, and neither replaces the other. Use the formal submission form rather than the questionnaire if you have a costed ask.

records.title: Finance committee pre-budget call for Budget 2027, expected window
records.body: Not open as of 3 September 2026. FINA's current studies still show the 2026 cycle, which closed 30 April 2026. The window shown here is inferred from the last two cycles. Watch FINA news releases rather than assuming.
records.tip: The Finance committee caps pre-budget briefs at 2,000 words and everything counts, including graphs, footnotes and quotes. One brief per organization or individual, on the committee template. Draft it now: the call is short and the cap is the binding constraint.

records.title: Science and Innovation Advisory Council, members not yet named
records.body: Committed in ISED's 2026-27 Departmental Plan, chaired by the Minister of Industry and supported by the Chief Science Advisor. No members named as of 3 September 2026. A body is most open between announcement and appointment.
records.tip: Both dates here are estimates, because no appointment date has been published. Send the Minister of Industry's office and the Office of the Chief Science Advisor a one-page case for the expertise the council will otherwise lack, and name two or three others who should sit on it. Re-verify before relying on this.

records.title: SRSR study: scientific information in French
records.body: The Standing Committee on Science and Research adopted this study of the External Advisory Panel report on 15 June 2026. No meetings held. The committee has requested a comprehensive government response under Standing Order 109. The witness list is unformed.
records.tip: No brief deadline is published. The close date shown is the last sitting day of the autumn 2026 period, 11 December 2026, not a committee deadline. With no meetings held, the scope and the witness list are both still open, so write to the clerk now rather than waiting.

records.title: SRSR study: Canada's dual use and defence research needs
records.body: Motion adopted 9 February 2026 on the role of universities, colleges, the National Research Council, industry and federal departments in dual use and defence research as a component of NATO spending targets. Ten briefs received, 29 witnesses heard, last meeting 11 June 2026.
records.tip: No brief deadline is published and the close date shown is the last sitting day of the autumn 2026 period. This study is well advanced, so a late brief must add something the 29 witnesses did not: a number, a comparative case, or workable wording for the research security rules.

records.title: FEWO study: labour force impacts of menopause and perimenopause
records.body: The Standing Committee on the Status of Women is taking briefs on the labour force impacts of menopause and perimenopause. Four briefs received, 11 witnesses heard, last meeting 16 June 2026.
records.tip: This study sets a hard limit the general rules do not: two pages, roughly 1,000 words, by 11:59 p.m. eastern on 30 September 2026. That is tighter than the ten-page House standard, so lead with the finding and the recommendation and cut the background entirely.

records.title: HESA study of Bill C-224, natural health products
records.body: Bill C-224, an Act to amend the Food and Drugs Act on natural health products, was read a second time and referred to the Standing Committee on Health. Forty-three briefs already received. No meetings held yet.
records.tip: No brief deadline is published and the close date shown is the last sitting day of the autumn 2026 period. Forty-three briefs are already in, so argue one clause and supply the wording, and find the member who will move it before clause-by-clause.

records.title: HESA study: Canada's pharmaceutical sovereignty
records.body: Self-initiated study by the Standing Committee on Health on domestic pharmaceutical capacity. Thirty-six briefs received, 28 witnesses heard, last meeting 7 May 2026.

records.title: NDDN study: Arctic transformation, security, defence and partnerships
records.body: The Standing Committee on National Defence is taking briefs on opportunities for security, defence and partnerships in the North. Three briefs received. No meetings held yet, so the scope and the witness list are still open.

records.title: NDDN study: Canadian Armed Forces recruitment and training programs
records.body: The Standing Committee on National Defence is taking briefs on recruitment and training. No meetings held yet and no briefs received, which is the earliest and most open point in a committee study.

records.title: Senate committees accept briefs on any active study, all year
records.body: Senate committees have no brief portal and no published deadlines. Briefs go by email to the committee clerk on any active study, and self-nomination as a witness is accepted. Lower volume and longer studies than the House.
records.tip: The official guide says a brief should generally not exceed ten pages, ideally five to ten, with a one-page executive summary if it runs longer. Send Word or PowerPoint rather than PDF so translation can work from it, and allow one business day per 2,000 words. A brief already sent to a House committee is not transferred: you must submit it to the Senate committee separately.

records.title: SSHRC Knowledge Synthesis Grants: the changing nature of security and conflict
records.body: Synthesis of existing research on a theme set with federal departments, not original research. Stream 1 pays $10,000 to $40,000 and stream 2 pays $10,000 to $78,000, over one year. Closes 8 p.m. eastern.
records.tip: Read the theme as intelligence about what departments are deciding, whether or not you apply. Your institution submits, so ask your research office for the internal deadline, which is always earlier. Contact the departments that co-set the theme directly, because no consultation on it has opened.

records.title: SSHRC Partnership Engage Grants, September 2026 competition
records.body: Short-term partnered research with a single public, private or not-for-profit organization, including a federal department. $10,000 to $50,000 over one year. The next competition after this one closes 15 December 2026.
records.tip: This is the most direct funded route into a federal department: one partner, one problem, one year. The partner letter is the part that cannot be assembled in the last week, so if you do not already have a named federal contact, aim at the December 2026 competition instead.

records.title: SSHRC Connection Grants, November 2026 competition
records.body: Short-term, targeted knowledge mobilization events and activities. $10,000 to $50,000 over one year. Four competitions run each year, so a missed deadline costs three months rather than a year.
records.tip: This is the one funding route that pays for the agenda-setting work itself: a workshop, a policy forum, a plain-language synthesis. Name the federal officials you intend to convene in the application, because a Connection Grant with public servants in the room is worth more than the money.
